_why: John, 12 Oct 2026 (Modes by kind of writing): a law code, a building plan, a debate, the Teacher's reflections, a collection of sayings, love poetry and visions each need their own summary shape, and in each the summary says whose words it gives. Which passages take which mode, and every fixed line a reader sees (settings, purposes, voices), are drafts here for John to approve once. Ranges follow the tN book outlines named in `source`. Nothing here is approved until status is 'approved' (rule 2). Approved by John on 12 Oct 2026. John approves; he is never cited as a source.

settings.line: Job’s friends argue that his suffering is punishment; at the end God says they were wrong (42:7).
settings.source: tN Job outline 7: “Yahweh rebukes Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar (42:7–9)”

settings.line: The Teacher looks at life “under the sun”, that is, on earth, and calls it vapor that quickly passes; his conclusion is to fear God and keep his commands.
settings.source: tN Ecclesiastes intro: “Under the sun” … “on the earth”; vapor “indicates transience”; “we must fear Yahweh and keep his commandments”

settings.line: Love poems in which a woman and a man speak to each other; the poem does not say who is speaking, so the speakers named here follow the UST’s headings.
settings.source: tN Song of Songs 1 intro: “the author does not identify the speakers … Before each speech, the UST places a header to identify the speaker”

settings.line: John writes down visions he was shown, told in symbols.
settings.source: tN Revelation intro: “John used a special style of writing to describe his visions. John described what he saw by using many symbols.”
